q.t: Find the distance between (0, 0) and (3, 4).
q.e: Distance formula is Pythagoras: √(3² + 4²).

q.t: Find the midpoint of (2, 4) and (6, 8).
q.e: Average the x’s and the y’s: ((2 + 6)/2, (4 + 8)/2).

q.t: In which quadrant does (−3, 5) lie?
q.e: x negative (left), y positive (up): the top-left quadrant.

q.t: Find the distance of (−6, 8) from the origin.
Every point on the x-axis has…
q.e: On the x-axis you have not moved up or down at all.

q.t: Find the distance between (1, 2) and (4, 6).
q.e: Differences 3 and 4: √(9 + 16).

q.t: Find the midpoint of (−2, 3) and (4, −1).
Find the distance between (a, 0) and (0, a).
Find the distance of (5, −12) from the origin.
Find the distance between (2, 3) and (4, 1).
q.e: Horizontal gap 2, vertical gap 2. By Pythagoras the distance is √(2² + 2²) = √8 = 2√2.

q.t: Find the point dividing the join of (2, 3) and (8, 9) in the ratio 1 : 2.
q.e: 1 : 2 means one-third of the way: (2 + 6/3, 3 + 6/3).

q.t: The distance between (x, 2) and (3, −2) is 5, with x > 3. Find x.
A point on the y-axis is equally far from (2, 3) and (−4, 1). Find its y-coordinate.
In what ratio does the x-axis divide the join of (2, −3) and (5, 6)?
q.e: On the x-axis y = 0: (6k − 3)/(k + 1) = 0 gives k = 1/2.

q.t: A(1, 2), B(4, 3), C(6, 6) are three vertices of parallelogram ABCD in order. Find D.
q.e: The diagonals bisect each other: D = A + C − B.

q.t: The midpoint of AB is (3, 4) and A = (1, 2). Find B.
q.e: B = 2 × midpoint − A.

q.t: Find the perimeter of the triangle with vertices (0, 0), (3, 0) and (0, 4).
Are the points (1, 5), (2, 3) and (−2, −11) collinear?
o: No — the two shorter distances do not add up to the longest
Yes — they lie on one line
Yes, because all the distances are different
You cannot tell without a graph
q.e: Distances: √5 ≈ 2.24, √212 ≈ 14.56 and √265 ≈ 16.28. If they were on one line, the two shorter distances would add up to the longest. But 2.24 + 14.56 = 16.80, not 16.28, so they form a triangle.

q.t: Find the point on the x-axis that is equally far from (2, −5) and (−2, 9).
q.e: A point on the x-axis is (x, 0). Square both distances and set them equal: (x − 2)² + 25 = (x + 2)² + 81, so −4x + 29 = 4x + 85 and x = −7.

q.t: Find the point that divides the join of (4, −3) and (8, 5) in the ratio 3 : 1.
q.e: Section formula: ((3 × 8 + 1 × 4)/4, (3 × 5 + 1 × (−3))/4) = (28/4, 12/4) = (7, 3). The point is 3/4 of the way, so nearer the second point.

q.t: What kind of triangle has vertices (3, 0), (6, 4) and (−1, 3)?
q.e: Sides 5, √50 and 5. Two equal sides, and 5² + 5² = 50, so a right angle.

q.t: Find the points that trisect the join of (1, −2) and (−3, 4).
q.e: Each third is (−4/3, 2). Step once and twice from (1, −2).

q.t: In what ratio does (1, 3) divide the join of (−1, 7) and (4, −3)?
q.e: x: (4k − 1)/(k + 1) = 1 gives k = 2/3. (y checks too.)

q.t: P(x, y) is equally far from (5, 1) and (1, 5). Which relation holds?
q.e: (x − 5)² + (y − 1)² = (x − 1)² + (y − 5)² simplifies to −8x + 8y = 0.

q.t: The distance between (a, 3) and (5, 7) is 5. Find a.
Do (1, 7), (4, 2), (−1, −1) and (−4, 4), taken in order, make a square?
o: Yes — four equal sides and equal diagonals
No — it is only a rhombus
No — it is only a rectangle
q.e: Each side squared is 34 (e.g. 3² + 5²), and both diagonals squared are 68. Equal sides make a rhombus; equal diagonals as well make it a square.

q.t: Q(0, 1) is equally far from P(5, −3) and R(x, 6). Find the positive value of x.
q.e: QP² = 25 + 16 = 41 and QR² = x² + 25. So x² = 16 and x = 4 (or −4).

q.t: In what ratio does the y-axis divide the join of (5, −6) and (−1, −4)?
q.e: Every point on the y-axis has x = 0. Take ratio k : 1: (k × (−1) + 5)/(k + 1) = 0, so k = 5. Ratio 5 : 1.

q.t: A = (3, 2) and B = (10, 9). P is on AB with AP = (3/7) AB. Find P.
The distance between (2, −3) and (10, y) is 10. Find y.
q.e: 8² + (y + 3)² = 10², so (y + 3)² = 36 and y + 3 = ±6. Both y = 3 and y = −9 work — two points on the vertical line x = 10.

q.t: A(−2, 0), B(2, 0) and C(0, k) form an equilateral triangle. Find k.
In what ratio does the line x − y − 2 = 0 divide the join of (3, −1) and (8, 9)?
q.e: The point ((8k + 3)/(k + 1), (9k − 1)/(k + 1)) must satisfy x − y = 2: 4 − k = 2k + 2.

q.t: A point on the x-axis is equally far from (3, 4) and (−1, 2). Find its x-coordinate.
Find the points that divide the join of (−4, 0) and (4, 8) into four equal parts.
q.e: Each quarter step is (2, 2).

q.t: Find the circumcentre of the triangle (8, 6), (8, −2), (2, −2).
q.e: The sides meet at right angles at (8, −2), so the circumcentre is the midpoint of the hypotenuse from (8, 6) to (2, −2).

q.t: Find the circumradius of the triangle (8, 6), (8, −2), (2, −2).
q.e: It is right-angled, so the radius is half the hypotenuse √(36 + 64) = 10.

q.t: (2, 1), (5, y), (x, 7) and (3, 6) are the vertices of a parallelogram in order. Find x + y.
q.e: The diagonals share a midpoint: 2 + x = 5 + 3 gives x = 6, and 1 + 7 = y + 6 gives y = 2.

q.t: (x, y) is equally far from (3, 6) and (−3, 4). Which relation holds?
q.e: (x − 3)² + (y − 6)² = (x + 3)² + (y − 4)². The x² and y² cancel: −6x − 12y + 45 = 6x − 8y + 25, so 12x + 4y = 20, i.e. 3x + y − 5 = 0.

q.t: The midpoint of A(2a, 4) and B(−2, 3b) is M(1, 2a + 1). Find a and b.
A lies on the join of P(6, −6) and Q(−4, −1) with PA/PQ = 2/5. A also lies on the line 3x + k(y + 1) = 0. Find k.
